items.rationale: Sections 2.4.4 and 7.1.9 cover like-for-like renewal of the frost-fractured valve. The same-wording reference supports €52 gross for one valve.
Section 7.1.9 covers the hose if it had to be renewed with the fractured valve. The same-wording reference supports €27 gross for one hose.
Sections 7.1.7(f) and 7.1.9 cover necessary repair labour. The reference rate of about €98 gross per hour gives €295 for the three-hour line, rounded.

Sections 3.6(c) and 7.1.7(e) distinguish actual repair consumables from general shop supplies. The generic billing and unpaid references make separate payment uncertain; €8 allows for a small quantity of documented consumables.
Sections 7.1.9 and 7.1.11 allow one attendance for the covered repair. The same-wording reference supports €41 gross for this visit.

Sections 2.4.6 and 5.2.2 expressly cover imaging equipment used to trace the leak, but the references make a separate equipment charge less certain. Estimate €25 for incremental use if separately payable, below the €2,500 gross event cap.
Section 7.1.11 excludes a return attendance by the same plumber unless agreed in advance, and no approval is reported. If approval were established, one trip is estimated at €41 gross.

items.description: Removal of loose and spalled plaster
items.rationale: The facade frost endorsement activates §2.6.2, which covers stripping failed material from the damaged area. Allow €90 gross for the two small removal units, excluding separately billed disposal.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(d) cover like-for-like base plaster on the frost-damaged area. Allow €45 gross for the material needed for local patching, without duplicating billed labour.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(c) cover re-forming the damaged substrate. Allow €105 gross for localized making good to the extent it is distinct from the base plaster and hourly labour lines.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(d) cover primer needed for the original finish system on the damaged area. Allow €30 gross for the local primer requirement, with labour billed separately.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(c) cover drying only where necessary before reinstatement. Allow €65 gross for a modest drying measure if a separate intervention was needed rather than ordinary curing time.

Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(d) pay only for the coats the like-for-like finish system requires on the damaged area. Allow €85 gross for ordinary finish materials without assuming all four billed coats were necessary.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(f) cover labour on the damaged elevation, not the separately billed rear repaint. Five hours at €65 gross per hour gives €325 for the line.

Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.8 cover necessary access; the scaffold served only the damaged elevation and was struck before rear work. About 48 m² at €13.50 gross per m² gives approximately €650 for ordinary hire, erection and dismantling.
Sections 2.6.3(a), 7.1.5 and 7.1.6 exclude repainting a separate undamaged elevation, even for a colour match. The €550 figure is a conditional gross estimate only, not an allowance.
Sections 2.6.2 and 5.2.1 cover disposal of material removed from the insured frost-damaged area. A few rubble sacks warrant about €55 gross for handling and disposal.
Sections 3.6(b) and 7.1.12 exclude a separate administration fee because it prices no repair work. The €10 figure is a conditional estimate only.
Sections 3.6(a) and 7.1.12 exclude crew subsistence even when the work itself is covered. The conditional estimate is three portions at €8 gross each, or €24.
